text:
ops-bot: ALERT: anomaly detector triggered for embeddings.edge.redwood-prod — sustained request surge from small IPv4 set, 95th pctl latency up, 5xx increasing. src ASN cluster: 7713, seen across 3 distinct /24s. auto-throttle engaged (soft).

mia: oncall here, looking now. can we get source IPs and country?

ops-bot: src_ips: 45.79.12.0/24, 45.79.13.0/24, 45.79.14.0/24; geo: EU/DE majority. peak 120k rps -> 18k rps after soft throttle.

samir: add to ipset blocklist and elevate rate-limit for embeddings route. pushing quick ACL via edge control plane now.

leah: recommend WAF rule to block the specific bursts (pattern: small POSTs with identical body fingerprint, embedding requests). also want a temporary per-customer token cap at 50 req/s while we triage.

mia: Samir — can you share the exact commands you run so I can replicate in the dedicated clusters?

samir: running (edge control plane):
```
edgectl acl create --name ddos-evasive-45-79 --action block --ipset "45.79.12.0/24,45.79.13.0/24,45.79.14.0/24"
edgectl ratelimit update --route "/v1/embeddings" --burst 200 --rate 50
```
Applying now to hosted and dedicated pools.

ops-bot: edgectl events: ACL applied to hosted region eu-central; rate-limit adjusted. observed client RPS dropped to ~9k. 5xx rate falling.

leah: WAF rule (temporary):
```
if request.path == "/v1/embeddings" and request.method == "POST" and body.size < 300 then block
```
Deploying as monitor-first for 2 minutes then block.

mia: support-ops, start pre-breach comms: no customer data impact, degraded embedding throughput for some EU requests. draft a short status note.

support-ops: draft: "We experienced elevated traffic against our embeddings endpoint from a small set of abusive IPs. We applied mitigations (edge ACL + WAF rule) and are monitoring. No evidence of data exfiltration; customers may see increased latency or throttling. Will update in 30m." OK to send? :eyes:

leah: Ack. Also: we need an audit trail for the ACL/WAF change and the ratelimit tweak — record who applied RBAC-scoped actions and ensure KMS usage logs show no suspicious key operations.

security-oncall: I pulled KMS logs — no unusual key decrypt/encrypt counts. But note: the operator who applied the ACL used the emergent "edge-admin" role. we'll add an audit entry and escalate to change-control to create a scoped "ddos-mitigator" role with limited scope so we don't need full edge-admin next time.

mia: good call. action items: 1) support send comms (support-ops) 2) Samir follow up with ipset blacklist propagation to Dedicated pools 3) Leah create a short WAF rule playbook + example. 4) Security create RBAC change request + audit log entry. 5) Post-incident: consider automated ASN blocking for repeated patterns.

samir: propagation started to dedicated: confirmed on two test hosts. will script propagation and post PR to infra repo.

ops-bot: monitoring update 00:05 later — RPS stabilized ~2k, 5xx almost back to baseline.

david: product flag — should we expose token-level rate-limit config to customers or keep it internal? leaning internal for now but want ops suggestions.

mia: internal for now, but add product ticket to evaluate customer-shielding controls in the console (RBAC + token caps).

support-ops: sent status update to affected customers, flagged high-touch accounts for outreach.

leah: postmortem notes starter: capture detection rule thresholds, false positive tuning, WAF rule template, RBAC role request, KMS audit confirmation, and consequences for billing / throttling.

security-oncall: I'll own RBAC change request and attach KMS audit snippet. please add any logs to the incident channel thread for retention.

mia: closing the live triage — keep thread for postmortem. thanks all. :thumbsup:
